copyright: Blue sunbeds on a sandy beach in Vai, Crete, Greece (© borchee/Getty Images)
description: On the remote northeastern tip of Crete, Greece, lies a quiet corner far from typical tourist routes. Today's image shows Vai Beach, a broad curve of golden sand bordered by calm, shallow waters of the Aegean Sea. With sunbeds, umbrellas and showers, it's ideal for swimming, relaxing or enjoying the peaceful atmosphere. But what truly sets Vai apart is just beyond the sand: Europe's largest natural palm grove. It consists of more than 5,000 Cretan date palm trees, a species native to Crete and parts of Turkey.

copyright: Aerial view of land and ocean, Victoria, Australia (© Nearmap/Getty Images)
description: Victoria, a southeastern state of Australia, extends along more than 1,100 miles of mainland coastline shaped by the Southern Ocean. From above, its beaches appear as sweeping bands of pale sand edged by turquoise waters and rugged cliffs. This dynamic interaction of land and sea defines much of the region's appeal. The famous Great Ocean Road traces roughly 150 miles of this shoreline, winding past popular surf spots, forested headlands and seaside towns.

copyright: Marie Lake, John Muir Wilderness near Bishop, California, United States (© Steve Dunleavy/Getty Images)
description: If mountains could keep a record of the past, the John Muir Wilderness near Bishop, California, United States, would have plenty to share. Its valleys, lakes and granite formations reveal a history shaped over millions of years. Established in 1964, this vast protected area spans more than 650,000 acres (263,000 hectares) of the Sierra Nevada and is named after naturalist John Muir. Today, parts of the Pacific Crest Trail and John Muir Trail pass through the area, drawing hikers into one of the largest high-elevation wilderness regions in the contiguous United States.

copyright: Lemon shark pup in mangrove forest, Eleuthera, Bahamas (© Shane Gross/Nature Picture Library)
description: On 14 July, Shark Awareness Day asks us to trade movie panic for ocean truth. Sharks have patrolled the seas for more than 420 million years, and as apex predators, they help keep marine ecosystems in balance.

copyright: Antelope Canyon on the Navajo Nation, east of Page, Arizona, United States (© Mark Skalny/Getty Images)
description: International Rock Day, observed on 13 July, celebrates the geological building blocks beneath our feet and encourages curiosity about how rocks shape Earth's landscapes and history. From the dramatic cliffs of Britain's coastline to vast desert canyons abroad, rocks reveal stories of ancient seas, shifting continents and life over millions of years.

copyright: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, Maine, United States (© Cavan Images/Offset/Shutterstock)
copyrightKeyword: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument
description: If you're looking for Maine in the United States at its wildest, Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument is hard to beat. Covering around 35,400 hectares of the North Woods, it is a landscape of quiet ponds, winding rivers and dense forests where nature still dominates.

copyright: Port de Saint-Goustan, Auray, Brittany, France (© Rolf E. Staerk/Shutterstock)
description: In France, Port de Saint-Goustan lies just below Auray’s upper town, where a narrow inlet meets the estuary leading into the Gulf of Morbihan. The harbour sits along the Auray River In the 13th century, the Dukes of Brittany built a bridge, a port and a castle here; the fortress has vanished, but cobbled quays and timber-framed houses still line the waterfront.
